paper_excerpt: PermWorld is a data platform of exact functions on permutations, annotated with answer relationships, joint reconstructions, input-query requirements, and verification status. It distinguishes mathematical derivability, source learning, and benefits from target adaptation. In an eight-unit Transformer experiment, deficiencies outperforms a specified comparison source by +8.7601 percentage points in weighted accuracy (95% paired t interval [+4.6823, +12.8378]). Its gain over scratch is +1.7670 points; the other comparison conditions exhibit negative transfer. A separate eight-unit GRU replication yields +3.1235 points with interval [-1.2743, +7.5213], leaving the primary effect uncertain. In a separate three-unit experiment, LDS complement-readout accuracy rises from 85.19% to 99.09% with additional pretraining, while direct LIS adaptation falls from 56.80% to 53.78%. Development-only calibration retains weakly learned and decoding-limited tasks, and an earlier background-interaction confirmation remains unsuccessful. These conditional findings separate available mathematical information from learned predictions and adaptation benefits; they do not establish internal formula use or a general transfer law.

source_excerpt: Skill-It is the closest methodological comparison for task dependencies. Its synthetic LEGO and digit-addition tasks have known generative structure. A skill is defined through a data slice and a learning response. Its formal dependency criterion compares the data needed to reach a specified metric: a uniform pair mixture must require no more data than target-only training. The graph estimators instead compare fixed-budget loss changes, then guide sampling. Thus synthetic tasks, task relations and budgeted selection are established prior work. A Skill-It training-response edge concerns learning under a procedure; a PermWorld answer identity specifies a reconstruction independent of model training. [Chen et al., 2023, Section 3, Definition 2 and Appendix C.2](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/70b8505ac79e3e131756f793cd80eb8d-Paper-Conference.pdf); [official synthetic generators and training interface](https://github.com/HazyResearch/skill-it/tree/807b3bf7b11970f3a6fb6201cb37dcc1a3335f00).

witnesses; allowing all registered I/R/C queries makes D and T sufficient in

model, not mathematically independent of FP. Missing relation annotations do

paper_excerpt: Every position falls into exactly one of equality, excess, or deficiency. Consequently, FP(p) = n - D(p) - D(inverse(p)). This registered reconstruction requires both specified deficiency queries: D(p) alone does not recover the target. Likewise, FP(p) = AF(complement(p)) for anti-fixed points AF, and LIS(p) = LDS(complement(p)). These are statements about answers; none asserts that a model implements the reconstruction.

source_excerpt:
- `position_partition`: `fixed_points(p) = n - exceedances(p) - deficiencies(p)`. Two same-input source answers and the known input length suffice.

- `lis_from_rsk_first_row` and `lds_from_rsk_first_column`: the full RSK shape determines both scalars, but the reverse implication does not follow.

source_excerpt: Both budgets use exactly the same source-training pool: 4096 objects per repeat and length, or 8192 total, not eight times as much independent data. A task may not have seen the entire pool at 4M, especially at k16. The 32M run can both increase that task's coverage of the fixed pool and repeat previously seen task-input pairs; not every additional example is a repeated task-input pair. source_excerpt:
The primary **+8.7601 pp is a comparison with U**, not a gain
of that size over random initialization. D's mean gain over shared A is
**+1.7670 pp**, sample SD 1.3512, with
7/8 positive units and 1 tie.

Thus the primary separation includes U's negative transfer relative to A as
well as D's smaller gain over A. This is a descriptive decomposition, not a
mechanistic or causal mediation result.

paper_excerpt: The budget study compares 4M and 32M nonpadding sequence tokens at k=2 and k=16 within each of two specified source chains. Here k counts nonconstant source-task instances after removing complete same-input aliases, not independent mathematical capabilities or templates. Both budgets start from paired random initialization and use the same relative-budget schedule, so their absolute-token learning-rate trajectories differ. Each repeat uses the same 8192-object source pool at both budgets. More budget can increase task-specific coverage and repeated exposure; it does not add the same proportion of independent data. The contrasts combine composition, exposure, and optimization conditions rather than isolating a pure task-count cause.
source_excerpt: k counts nonconstant task instances after removing exact same-input aliases, not independent mathematical information. The pool has 24 instances from 22 templates. Every prefix has distinct templates, so its template count also equals k. Two nested chains have different membership at every k. Their broad family counts match: cycle/subsequence at k=2; one cycle/subsequence/block/legacy instance at k=4; two of each at k=8; and 4/3/4/5 at k=16. The k=2 sets consequently do not cover every family. Definitions and membership were frozen before training, using no transfer outcome.
